title.narrative: DocudaysUA International Documentary Human Rights Festival 2021-2024
DocudaysUA International Documentary Human Rights Festival 2021-2024

description.narrative:
Civilsamhällsorganisationen "Docudays", har samarbetat med Sverige sedan 2012. Det började för över femton år sedan som en liten Kherson-baserad civilsamhällesorganisation som drevs av entusiaster, som sedan växte till en medelstor organisation vars verksamhet sträckte sig bortom huvudstaden, för att slutligen bli en erkänd nationell plattform för mänskliga rättigheter.
DocudaysUA är en del av programmet för civilsamhällesstöd vid Sveriges ambassad i Kiev. Detta programbaserade stöd till civilsamhällesorganisationer syftar till att stärka deras organisatoriska kapacitet för att bli mer effektiva och transparenta och därmed kunna leverera bättre resultat.
Under 2019-2020 har organisationen fått stöd från ambassaden på 12 MSEK för att stärka organisationens utveckling i linje med en effektivitetsrevision som gjordes av konsultföretaget ’NGC’ i slutet av 2018. Utöver detta har organisationen framgångsrikt genomfört sin stora programaktivitet – en årlig internationell dokumentärfestival för mänskliga rättigheter i Kiev och med en landsomfattande turné i slutet av varje år. Syftet med detta stöd är att fortsätta att stärka Docudays som institution så att den kan fortsätta spela en huvudroll som förändringskraft för att vårda kulturen för tolerans, icke-diskriminering, acceptans och jämlikhet, samtidigt som det skapar bredare tillgång till högkvalitativa dokumentärer om mänskliga rättigheter som används som slagverktyg för att utveckla kritiskt tänkande och göra Ukraina till en verklig demokratisk stat. Respekten för de mänskliga rättigheterna och fullt åtnjutande av grundläggande rättigheter och friheter, jämställdhet mellan könen och beslutfattares förståelse av de mänskliga rättigheterna är fortfarande viktiga frågor i Ukraina. Att uppmärksamma kränkningar av mänskliga rättigheter, diskriminering och hatbrott, samt att utbilda allmänheten om mänskliga rättighetsfrågor, är projektets bidrag till Ukrainas väg mot mer europeiska värderingar och normer.
Stödet är helt i linje med resultatstrategin för Sveriges reformsamarbete med Östeuropa, västra Balkan och Turkiet 2014 - 2021. Festivalen ger synlighet till det svenska reformsamarbetet och är nära kopplat till annat arbete för mänskliga rättigheter. Publik från kriminalvårdsinstitutioner och socialtjänsten engagerar sig i diskussioner, seminarier och kurser om olika frågor om livet i Ukraina, inklusive jämställdhet, miljö, konfliktlösning, mänskliga rättigheter etc. Cirka 300 skolor avser engagera sig i Docudays nationella anti-mobbningskampanj. Ytterligare ett svenskt regionalt stöd, ’B2B Doc’, vars mål är att öka kapaciteten hos dokumentärfilmskapare i Ukraina, Moldavien, Vitryssland, Georgien och Armenien, har byggts in i festivalens arkitektur. Under 2019-2020 utvecklade och antog organisationen mycket ny policy som nu kommer att vävas in i organisationen ytterligare. Detta innebär att organisationen under 2021 kommer att fortsätta arbeta med att implementera och slutföra rekommendationerna från den verifieringsrevision som genomfördes i december 2020.
Med anledning av ovanstående fattas ett beslut att utvidga ett treårigt programstöd till Docudays CSO av ambassaden.

The civil society organization "Docudays" CSO, has been a long-standing partner of Sweden since 2012. Starting as a small Kherson-based enthusiasts-driven CSO over a decade and a half ago, the organization, with a secondary office located in Kyiv, grew to a mid-sized NGO whose activities did not only limit within the capital, but eventually became a recognized national human rights platform.
DocudaysUA is benefiting from the Civil Society Development Programme of the Embassy of Sweden in Kyiv. This is programme-based support to civil society organizations to strengthen their organizational capacities in order to become more efficient and transparent and, as a consequence, capable of delivering better results. During 2019-2020, the organization has enjoyed a support from the Embassy of 12 MSEK to, firstly, strengthen the organizational development of the organization in line with an efficiency audit by the NCG consultancy carried out in late 2018. Secondly, the organization has successfully accomplished its major programme activity - annual international documentary human rights festival in Kyiv and with a follow-up country-wide roadshow at the end of each year.
The purpose of this intervention is to continue strengthening Docudays as an institution so it may continue to play a key role as a change agent in nurturing the culture of tolerance, non-discrimination, acceptance and equality, while creating more opportunities for the readily-available, accessible, comprehensive, and inclusive access to high-quality human rights documentary films that are used as impact tools to develop critical thinking and make Ukraine a genuine democratic state. The respect for human rights and full enjoyment of basic rights and fundamental freedoms, gender equality, understanding of human rights by the duty bearers still remains an issue in Ukraine. To draw attention to violations of human rights, discrimination and abuse, including hate crimes and to educate the general public on human rights issues is the project contribution to the country's progress towards EU values and norms.
The support is fully in line with the Result Strategy for Sweden's reform cooperation with Eastern Europe, Western Balkans and Turkey 2014 - 2021. The festival provides visibility to Swedish Reform Cooperation and is closely linked to other human rights work. The audience from the penitentiary institutions, social services units is being engaged into discussions, round table, seminars and master classes on the many difficult issues of life in Ukraine, including gender equality, environment, conflict resolution, human rights, etc. About 300 schools have expressed their intention to engage with Docuday’s National Anti-Bullying Campaign, while another Swedish regional intervention B2B Doc whose goal is to enhance the capacities of documentary filmmakers in Ukraine, Moldova, Belarus, Georgia, and Armenia, has been built into the Festival’s architecture.
During 2019-2020 the organization developed and adopted a bulk of policies and procedures which will now be further integrated and internalized. This implies that the organization during 2021 will continue to work with implementing and finalizing the recommendations of the verification audit conducted in December 2020. Against this background, a decision to extend a three year-long programme support to Docudays CSO is made by the Embassy.

Evaluation and summary of the results
2021 Summary and Analysis
Key Achievements:
Engagement and Reach: Directly engaged 475,283 participants across Ukraine through various activities, including film screenings, discussions, human rights campaigns, and workshops.
Inclusion: Pioneered accessibility features such as audio description for visually impaired individuals and open captions for the hearing impaired during the International Human Rights Documentary Film Festival Docudays UA and DOCU/CLUB Network events.
Recognition: Received an award at the III International Inclusion Forum for developing an inclusive society in In 2021, the 18th Docudays UA International Human Rights Documentary Film Festival became a finalist in the the Peace category of the UN Global Compact competition Partnership for Sustainable Development 2021
Innovation: DOCU/CLUB Network piloted a new activity: organized 50 locally driven advocacy campaigns with local authorities across Ukraine to address local The activity brought remarkable results in activating the communities and bringing actual changes for the better.
Festival Highlights: The 18th International Human Rights Documentary Film Festival featured 105 films from 37 countries, attracting significant online engagement with 115,899 views and 77 guests from 12 countries.
Building organizational capacity: In 2021, DOCUDAYS continued strengthening its role in building civil society, developing civic engagement in Ukraine, protecting human rights, and promoting human dignity as the highest To a large extent, this was made possible due to the consistent institutional development and improvement of the organizational capacity of the DOCUDAYS, in particular, in the context of lockdowns. Updating and implementing important policies (Procurement Policy, Anti-Corruption Policy; Human Resources Management Policy), constant training of team members, development of clear provisions, regulations, and procedures, effective distribution of tasks and responsibilities, establishing an internal communications system, developing an external communications strategy, monitoring the success of individual areas of the organization's activities - all this helped to improve the organization's performance. In addition, DOCUDAYS has identified a new vector of activity for itself - the development of a sustainable development strategy and the implementation of an environmental and social approach in the organizations existing and future projects. In December, the team was trained with an introductory lecture on the concept of sustainable development and the need for a sustainable development strategy for an organization with an environmental and social impact assessment.
Analysis: 2021 was marked by extensive outreach and a strong emphasis on inclusivity. The organization successfully adapted to online formats, increasing its accessibility and engagement despite the challenges posed by the pandemic. The award for inclusivity and the large number of participants reflected positively on DOCUDAYS' commitment to inclusion and human rights.
2022 Summary and Analysis
Key Achievements:
Adaptation to Wartime Conditions: In 2022, amidst the Russian invasion of Ukraine, DOCUDAYS demonstrated exceptional resilience by quickly adapting its operations to continue supporting civil society and human Despite the drastic circumstances, the organization ensured the continuity of its activities by adjusting communication strategies and launching new initiatives to bolster Ukraines efforts during the war. These included rapid response projects and activities tailored to the wartime context (such as the Ukraine War Archive, cultural diplomacy efforts, adjusted operation of the DOCU/CLUB Network, and DOCU/HELP fundraising initiative, adapted theme and format of the 19th Docudays UA film festival in Kyiv and 19 Travelling Docudays UA festival in regions).
Effective organizational management: The organization maintained robust internal communication despite team members being dispersed across various locations due to the full-scale Russian This facilitated coordinated efforts and sustained organizational effectiveness during significant disruption.
Maintaining a cohesive operational structure in such a turbulent environment highlights the strength and adaptability of the DOCUDAYS team. Building the capacity of our team is one of our key values. That is why, despite the challenges of martial law, the Docudays Team continued to implement the Human Resource Development Plan. 38 members of the DOCUDAYS team took various professional development courses in 2022, including improving the level of foreign languages; crisis management; fundraising; digital accessibility and sustainable cultural development; special training as part of the implementation of the Ukraine War Archive project on war crimes, tagging in a digital database, and principles of interviewing victims of war crimes."
Expanding international outreach: In 2022, DOCUDAYS, in response to the challenges of the full-scale invasion, strongly enhanced its outreach to new international Docudays UA represented Ukraine at 59 international events in 18 countries, including the Cannes Film Festival, IDFA, Sheffield Doc/Fest, Krakow Film Festival, Triennale Milano, and others. Representatives of the DOCUDAYS team spoke abroad about Ukraines identity and emphasized the need to debunk Russias imperial narratives.
Course to sustainable development: held internal audit on sustainable development and made a Roadmap for further development of the sustainable development strategy and policies.
Recognition: In 2022, DOCUDAYS was honored with the FilmAid Award (by global NGO Internews) for its outstanding contributions to promoting human rights through films.
Analysis: 2022 was dominated by the challenge of operating during wartime. DOCUDAYS demonstrated remarkable resilience and adaptability, ensuring its activities supported Ukrainian civil society and human rights in response to the crisis. This period underscored the organization's agility and dedication to its mission under extraordinary circumstances.
2023 Summary and Analysis
Key Achievements:
Expanding the scale of program activities: In 2023, despite the remaining challenges of wartime, the scope and scale of program activities approached those of the pre-COVID period. For example, the anniversary 20 Docudays UA festival reached 25,479 people, while the number of film clubs in the DOCU/CLUB Network amounted to 425 fully operational units. Credible digital database: for two years of Ukraine War Archive activity, the team has collected and analyzed around 9 million digital materials, made detailed analytics and tagging of over 25,000 materials, and registered 36,000 war events and potential war crimes. Our team has recorded 670 unique interviews with war crime witnesses and produced the first short episode of the documentary series Witnesses. The UWA has the potential of becoming a single secure and user-friendly database of the Russian-Ukraine full-scale war being a real helper for researchers, investigators, media, historians, artists, international organizations, state entities, and many other professional communities.
External Evaluation: DOCUDAYS underwent an external evaluation by Tana Copenhagen, highlighting the organization's ability to meet the dynamic expectations of civil society and The evaluation praised DOCUDAYS for effectively adapting to the COVID-19 pandemic and the full-scale invasion.
Strategic Planning: the Docudays Team held a strategic session and developed a new strategic plan for 2024-2026 with a revised set of activities in response to the wartime context.
Monitoring and Evaluation: Implemented systematic M&E systems, including audience surveys at festivals, showing an increased interest in cultural events and the effectiveness of documentary films as a communication tool.
Recognition: The Ukraine War Archive received the Responsibility Award 2023 of the Bohdan Hawrylyshyn Family Foundation in the category "Interaction without Borders: Ukraine to the " The Ukraine War Archive became finalist in the category Warriors of light in the Partnership for Sustainability Award 2023 by UN Global Compct.
Analysis: In 2023, DOCUDAYS focused on expanding the program operations, strategic growth, and The external evaluation validated its adaptive strategies and effective operations. The emphasis on systematic M&E and strategic planning signifies a mature and forward-looking organization. The active fundraising efforts indicate a strong drive towards financial stability and expanded impact.
Overall Analysis
Broad Participation: Over the three-year period, DOCUDAYS directly engaged 704,051 participants across Ukraine and over 1.5 mln with its communication efforts. This extensive engagement was facilitated through a diverse array of activities, including film screenings, discussions, human rights and advocacy campaigns, and workshops. These efforts significantly broadened the organizations reach and impact across different demographics and regions, including beyond Ukraine.
Adapting to Digital Formats: During the COVID-19 pandemic, DOCUDAYS adeptly transitioned many of its activities to online formats, ensuring continued participation and engagement. For instance, the 18th International Human Rights Documentary Film Festival in 2021 featured 105 films from 37 countries and achieved substantial online engagement with 115,899 views. This adaptation not only maintained but also enhanced participation levels when in-person events were restricted, demonstrating the organization's ability to innovate and remain relevant.
Innovative Accessibility Features: DOCUDAYS has been at the forefront of inclusivity, implementing pioneering accessibility features. These include audio descriptions for visually impaired individuals and open captions and sign language interpretation for the hearing impaired during its events. Throughout the project, the accessibility elements continued to increase, and the 20 Docudays UA festival already featured 100% films with open captions, 10 films with audio description, and 17 events with sign language interpretation). These measures ensured cultural and educational content was accessible to a broader audience, reflecting DOCUDAYS commitment to inclusivity.
Resilience and Adaptation: Over the past three years, DOCUDAYS has demonstrated exceptional resilience and adaptability. This was particularly evident during the pandemic and the ongoing war in Ukraine. The organizations ability to maintain and even expand its operations under such challenging conditions underscores its robust operational framework and the dedication of its team. The swift adaptation to digital formats and crisis conditions ensured that DOCUDAYS continued to fulfill its mission and reach its audience effectively.
Strategic Focus: DOCUDAYS has consistently worked on strategic planning and development. By revising its mission statement, developing comprehensive strategic plans, and conducting strategic training, the organization has ensured its goals and activities remain relevant and impactful in an ever-changing environment. The CSO continued to improve our sustainable approaches to management and project activities, taking into account the 17 UN Sustainable Development Goals and the social, economic, and environmental aspects of our activities. The detailed planning for future years and alignment of financial resources with strategic objectives highlight a mature and forward-thinking approach.
Conclusion
Over the past three years, DOCUDAYS has made significant strides in expanding its reach, enhancing inclusivity, and maintaining robust operations despite facing considerable COVID and wartime challenges. The organizations strategic planning, resilience, and commitment to inclusivity have been key to its continued success and impact. Through innovative approaches and a steadfast dedication to its mission, DOCUDAYS has not only adapted to but also thrived in a dynamic and often difficult environment, making substantial contributions to building civil society and human rights in Ukraine. The comprehensive planning, proactive fundraising, and effective crisis response measures position DOCUDAYS as a resilient and impactful organization aimed at continued success and growth.
The successful development of our organization, its projects and programs is largely due to the support of the Sida and the Embassy of Sweden in Ukraine, both financial and expert. While cooperating with the Embassy of Sweden in Ukraine since 2013, the CSO have learned many important things: to think ten steps ahead, to plan and reflect carefully, to always act for the best result, to make constant progress in building the organization and in the direction of institutional and sustainable development.
